what: In-context sound power of each orchestral part at its written dynamic, against the map's implied per-player level (sectionLevel2's Clark & Luce real side + realRange 2's steps): research only, not read by any generator or by MuseScore. docs/RESEARCH.md > 1.5a.

sources.aalto: Paetynen, Pulkki & Lokki 2008, "Anechoic recording system for symphony orchestra", Acta Acustica u. Acustica 94(6) 856-865; Lokki, Paetynen & Pulkki 2008, "Recording of anechoic symphony music", Acoustics 08 Paris (mic positions, Table 1). research.cs.aalto.fi/acoustics/virtual-acoustics/research/acoustic-measurement-and-analysis/85-anechoic-recordings.html: "The recordings are all made with exactly the same gain settings". MP3 192 kb/s, front mic 6 (az 0, el 10.8, 2.30 m from the player's head), horns also mic 8 (az 144, 1.92 m), bassoons / tuba also mic 5 (az 288, el 52.6, 2.49 m). One professional player per instrument (Finnish orchestras) played every part. Licence: "free for academic research"; derived numbers only.
sources.phenicx: Miron, Carabias-Orti, Bosch, Gomez & Janer 2016, PHENICX-Anechoic note annotations (Zenodo 840025, CC BY 4.0): bar timing only.
sources.tub8: Boehm, Ackermann & Weinzierl 2020, "A Multi-channel Anechoic Orchestra Recording of Beethoven's Symphony No. 8 op. 93", J. Audio Eng. Soc. 68(12) 977-984, doi:10.17743/jaes.2020.0056; data doi:10.14279/depositonce-6729.2 (CC BY 4.0), the open excerpts of movements 1, 2, 4. Orchester Wiener Akademie (period instruments), recorded groupwise; 2 players per wind / violin / viola part, 1 cello, 1 bass. Every track normalised to 1 m and 10.1 mV/Pa: SPL at 1 m in the mic direction = dBFS + 94 + 49.8 - mic gain - artistic gain (Table 3; the paper's worked example), the engineer's artistic gain reversed.
sources.directivity: TU Berlin directivity database (Ackermann, Boehm, Brinkmann & Weinzierl 2024, doi:10.14279/depositonce-19858 v3, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: derived numbers only), 1a single tones (ff): DI toward each mic, p^2 interpolated over the 32 receivers (inverse squared angle, 4 nearest), mean over notes; modern instruments for Aalto, the classical-era ones for TU B8 (Violin/Viola/Cello/Double_bass_historical, Keyed_flute, Classic_oboe, Clarinet_historical, Classic_bassoon, Natural_horn, Natural_trumpet).

method: Score readings (bar:beat dynamics, hairpins, cresc./dim., accents, technique texts, notes spans per player) by agents from public-domain scores: anechoic_balance/readings/*.tsv. NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER (readings rule).
Envelope: 50 ms mean square after a 40 Hz high pass; a frame is active when over the track noise (5th percentile) + 10 dB and within 30 dB of its 99th percentile.

Steady segment: where the part plays, one written marking, more than 0.25 bar (TU / Mahler 0.4) inside the segment's ends, outside hairpins / cresc. / dim. (+-0.25 bar) and 0.05 bar before .. 0.25 bar after a point accent (sf, fp, ...), outside stopped horn / mutes / pizz. Level = power mean of its active frames less the noise power; repeated passes of one player power-averaged.
Lw = level + 20 log10(r) + 11 - DI(mic) (+ the dataset constant: unknown for Aalto, the calibration for TU B8); Aalto horns, bassoons, tuba: the dB mean of the two microphones' estimates.
Map's per-player Lw at a marking = Lw_mp (sso_cl_section_balance.json, one player) + markingSteps x realSteps / 5 (ContextLevel: pp -2, p -1, mp 0, mf 1, f 2, ff 3, fff 4).

r = Lw - map Lw per part x marking (frame-weighted energy mean of its segments); rel = r - the strings' mean r at the same marking in the same piece (at least two string parts, 10 s). rel < 0: the part plays softer against the strings in context than the map plays it.
Per instrument and dataset: median over part x marking values, bootstrap 90 % interval; pooled = the mean of the two datasets' medians (different players).
